A.text:
Two identical uniform spheres each of mass M and having radius R are separated by distance 4R between their centres.

A small particle of mass m is projected from one of the sphere along the line joining them such that it reaches to the other sphere. The minimum speed of projection is
A.sol_text:
Answer : (4)
Solution:
−GMm/R − GMm/(3R) + (1/2)mv² = (−GMm/(2R) − GMm/(2R))
⇒ (1/2)mv² = GMm/R + GMm/(3R) − GMm/R
⇒ v² = 2GM/(3R)
∴ v = √(2GM/(3R))

A.subject: Physics
A.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
A.text:
Two blocks each of mass m are connected by a relaxed spring having force constant k. The blocks rest on a smooth horizontal table. At time t = 0, the block on the left is given a sharp impulse J towards the right, and the block begin to slide along the table. The velocity of the left block as a function of time is
(where ω is angular speed of SHM)
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:

When impulse act on block A initially, velocity of block A and B are u_A = J/m, u_B = 0. Velocity of centre of mass is J/2m
In centre of mass frame
u_A = u_A - v_cm = J/2m
u_B = u_B - v_cm = -J/2m
In this frame blocks are performing SHM with angular speed
ω = √(k/(m·m/(m+m))) = √(2k/m)

At initial instant spring is relaxed therefore x_A/ICM = A sin(ωt) and x_B/ICM = A sin(ωt + π) Velocity of A in CM frame
u'_A = u_A cos ωt = (J/2m) cos ωt
In ground frame
V_A/g = u_A + V_CM = (J/2m)(1 + cos ωt)

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: The major product of the following reaction is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (3)
Solution:

The reaction sequence shows:

1. Starting material: 2-aminobiphenyl-4'-ol (ortho-amino group on one ring, para-hydroxy group on the other ring)

2. Step (i): NaNO₂, HCl, 0°C
   The amino group (NH₂) undergoes diazotization to form diazonium salt (N⁺≡NCl⁻) on the benzene ring

3. Step (ii): aq.NaOH
   In basic conditions, the diazonium group undergoes intramolecular nucleophilic aromatic substitution. The hydroxyl group (present on the adjacent ring) attacks the diazonium salt, leading to formation of a new C-N bond and formation of a benzimidazole ring system through cyclization.

4. The mechanism involves:
   - Activation of the OH group in basic conditions (O⁻ form)
   - The oxygen acts as a nucleophile and attacks the diazonium carbon
   - Loss of N₂ as a leaving group
   - Subsequent aromatization and rearrangement
   - Formation of a tricyclic system with a benzimidazole moiety (N=N ring fused to the biphenyl system)

5. Final product: The tricyclic compound with an N=N double bond forming a benzimidazole ring system with the hydroxyl group still attached to the phenyl ring, giving option (3)

A.sol_text:

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text:
Which options is/are correct about the major product formed in the following reaction and its mechanism?

Cl—CH₂—CH—CH₂ + C₂H₅ONa →
        ⁺ O⁻
options: Ethoxide ion attacks the epoxide ring at the secondary carbon
Ethoxide ion attacks the primary carbon attached to Cl.
The major product is CH₂—CH—CH₂—OCH₃ with O between CH₂ and CH
The major product is C₂H₅O—CH₂—CH—CH₂ with O between CH and CH₂
A.sol_text:
Cl—CH₂—CH—CH₂ + C₂H₅Õ
         O

↓

Cl—CH₂—CH—CH₂—OC₂H₅
        Õ

↓ (Õ attacks)

CH₂—CH—CH₂—OC₂H₅
   O

Answer: (3)
Solution:
The ethoxide ion attacks the epoxide ring at the secondary carbon (the CH carbon), which is the less hindered position. The Cl⁻ leaves first, and then the oxygen nucleophile attacks from the backside, leading to ring opening. A.subject: Mathematics
A.text: A variable straight line with slope 4 intersects the hyperbola xy = 1 at two points P and Q. The locus of a point which divides PQ in the ratio 1 : 2 is
A.sol_text:
Let P(t₁, 1/t₁) and Q(t₂, 1/t₂) let R (x, y) be a locus point.
Then 3x = 2t₁ + t₂ → (i)
3y = 2/t₁ + 1/t₂ ⇒ 2t₂ + t₁ = 3yt₁t₂ → (ii)
Slope of PQ = 4 ⇒ (1/t₂ - 1/t₁)/(t₂ - t₁) = 4
⇒ t₁t₂ = -1/4 → (iii)

⇒ 4t₁ + 8t₂ = -3y
From (i)

⇒ 16x² + 10xy + y² = 2

A.text: If sin² θ = (4−m²)/3, m ∈ [−2, −1] ∪ [1, 2] and cot³(θ/2) = cot α, then the value of cos²(α) + sin²(α) is equal to
A.sol_text:

⇒ sin³(θ/2)/cos³(θ/2) = sin α/cos α
⇒ sin³(θ/2)/sin α = cos³(θ/2)/cos α = k
Now, sin(θ/2) = (k sin α)^(1/3), cos(θ/2) = (k cos α)^(1/3)

Also, k²(sin² α + cos² α) = sin⁶(θ/2) + cos⁶(θ/2) = m²/4
k² = m²/4
∴ 1/k^(2/3) = (2/m)^(2/3)
